pool.note: Rows are the secret/stakes halves of one entry; the draw picks the pair, so a pair is admissible only when both halves are. The pool is the flatMap over EVERY active stress kind, so a line keyed by one kind can print beside another; the key guarantees only its own kind. {npc} rows declare other-npc (otherNpcOf's roster pick; the 'someone' fallback is the rung-2 failure the atom exists for). {faction}/{commodity} have renderer fallbacks: not atoms. 'the council' is declared ruler: council although an elder council would also satisfy the prose (rulerKind reads elder there): over-restrictive, never permissive. famine#1.secret presumes a flood (no atom); famine#2 presumes a regional authority above the place (no atom); wartime#2 presumes war contracts made the place rich (no atom); insurgency#6 and slave_revolt#6 presume underways/tunnels beneath the settlement (no atom); indebted#2.stakes/succession_void#4.stakes/infiltrated#1 also assign the other NPC a trade or office (notary, archivist) the roster may not give them (no atom). The source comment records DEFENSE-2's rewording: no line names garrison, soldiers or walls today.

rows.text: Secretly negotiating surrender terms with the besieging force, without the council's knowledge
Treason. The defenders would execute them on the spot if they found out
Has been rationing their own private food stores while publicly enforcing the communal rationing order
Two of the people enforcing the rationing know about the stores; they've been paid to look the other way
Passed information about the settlement's water supply to someone in the besieging camp three weeks ago
People have already died because of it; they've been living with that knowledge
Knows the barricade across the main approach is structurally compromised and has told no one
Telling the council means explaining why they knew and said nothing for two weeks
Has already made personal arrangements to leave before the final assault. Their family left last week
{npc} saw them loading the cart. They don't know what {npc} understood
The supplies they declared destroyed in a fire are actually hidden in a location only they know
People are starving. The supplies could last another month
Is in contact with the besieging commander (not as a spy, as a former colleague)
The relationship predates the siege. They've been using it to buy time, but the council would not accept the distinction
Authorised an illegal sortie that failed. Five people died and no record was kept
{npc} survived it. They know, and they've been drinking heavily ever since
Has been skimming from the {commodity} reserves to pay a personal debt that predates the siege
The shortage will be noticed when the final accounting is done. They're hoping they die before that happens
Controls a hidden cache of {commodity} reserves that could feed the settlement for two more weeks
{faction} suspects it. They've been watching the property
Sold the settlement's emergency grain reserves three months ago at peak price and reported them destroyed in a flood
The flood was real. The reserves were already gone. The paperwork is missing one date
Has been reporting false harvest figures to the regional authority to suppress aid that would undercut their price control
People have died. The regional inspector arrives in six days
Knows who is hoarding and has made a private arrangement to share the information, for a price
Both the hoarder and {faction} would move against them if either found out
Their family has been eating normally throughout the famine (not from stores, from a private source they will not name)
{npc} has noticed. They asked once. They were told to forget it
Helped engineer the original supply disruption that triggered the famine, believing it would only last a week
It has lasted six. They did not anticipate this. They cannot undo it. They cannot admit it
Is receiving {commodity} shipments through a covert route and selling them at triple the official price after dark
Three people know. One of them is already dead. The other two don't know about each other
Has documentation proving the famine was caused by export decisions made by {faction}, and has been paid to lose it
The documentation exists in another form. Somewhere
Has been feeding information to the occupation authority since the first week, not under duress
{npc} is part of the resistance. They trust this person completely
Made a private arrangement with the occupation commander that ensures their safety and their family's at the cost of three others' names
Those three people don't know why they were arrested
Was part of the original resistance but surrendered their entire cell's identities to avoid imprisonment
Some of them are still alive in the occupation's custody. They believe they were betrayed by someone else
Has been documenting occupation atrocities in secret, but for sale to the highest bidder, not for justice
{faction} would pay well. So would the occupation authority, to suppress it
Their position under the occupation exists because they helped legitimise the takeover (a public statement they made in the first week)
They were told it was just paperwork. They knew it wasn't
Is smuggling people out, but only those who can pay, and the price has been rising
{npc} can't pay. They've been waiting for weeks. The next group leaves in two days
Knows the occupation commander's real orders (not the stated ones), and those orders include a date
The date is soon. Telling anyone means explaining how they know
Has been playing both powers simultaneously, feeding each the other's plans
{faction} just sent someone to verify information that won't check out. The meeting is tomorrow
The vote that split the council was not actually close. They falsified the count
The original tallies still exist somewhere. {npc} was in the room
Has already agreed to support whichever power wins in exchange for a specific appointment they have not disclosed
They've made this offer to both sides. Both sides believe they have an exclusive commitment
Was responsible for the incident that triggered the fracture: an act of deliberate sabotage they've successfully blamed on the other power
One member of the power they framed knows the truth and has been building a case
Knows where the settlement's founding documents are (documents that would legally invalidate the current governing structure entirely)
They've been sitting on this information for eighteen months, waiting for the right moment
Their public neutrality is a cover. They are actively funding one faction's operations through a third party
{npc} traced one payment. They came to ask about it. They accepted the explanation. They didn't believe it
The debt was not authorised by the council. They signed alone under pressure and have been hiding it for two years
{faction} is about to discover this in the accounts they requested
Has been making personal side payments to the creditor's representative in exchange for delay notices that look official
The representative's records will be audited when the contract matures. In three months
Knows the debt contains a clause that transfers significant civic assets to the creditor on default (a clause that was buried in the original document)
{npc} is a notary who helped draft it. They've been avoiding eye contact for six months
Has been embezzling from civic funds to make personal debt payments, using the same creditor network for both
The two debts are about to merge in a way that will be impossible to explain separately
Sold privileged commercial information to a foreign merchant house to cover an interest payment (information that {faction} considers proprietary)
The merchant house used the information publicly. The source will be traced
The original {commodity} contract that created the debt was based on projections they knew were false at the time of signing
The creditor's representative has begun asking questions that suggest they've found the original projection documents
Has already transferred personal assets out of the settlement to a safe location, anticipating default and the personal liability that follows
{npc} helped with the transfer. They've said nothing. They're waiting to see what they get for their silence
They were the betrayer, not the person the investigation has been pursuing
The evidence against the other person is circumstantial but strong. Letting it proceed is the easiest thing in the world
Knows who did it and has said nothing. The betrayer is someone they owe a significant debt to
The debt is called in if they speak. The settlement suffers if they don't. They've been choosing themselves for six weeks
Participated in the original betrayal in a minor capacity and has been helping frame someone else ever since
{npc} saw them at a meeting they claimed not to attend. {npc} has not yet understood what they saw
Has the actual evidence of who committed the betrayal. They found it accidentally and immediately hid it
The evidence also implicates {faction}, which means the fallout would be much larger than anyone currently expects
Was approached before the betrayal and said no, but also said nothing to warn anyone, for reasons they still believe were defensible
If the investigation reaches them, the question of what they knew and when will end their career even if they're not charged
Has been meeting with someone whose affiliation they now suspect. They didn't know at the time, and stopping the meetings would confirm they suspect something
The information passed was minor. Or seemed minor. They're no longer certain
Noticed an inconsistency in {npc}'s behaviour three weeks ago and said nothing, deciding it was probably nothing
It was not nothing. And now they've waited too long to raise it without explaining why they waited
Their correspondence has been read (by whom, they don't know), but the evidence is there for anyone paying attention
The correspondence contains something that would end their career if taken out of context. It will be taken out of context
Is the infiltrator, placed by an outside interest before the settlement's current leadership took power
Their handler has not made contact in four months. They don't know if that means the operation is over or if something has changed
Was recruited by the infiltrating party a year ago and has been passing low-level information, telling themselves it doesn't matter
They were recently asked for something that does matter. They said yes
Knows the disease's origin and has been suppressing that information to protect someone they care about
The outbreak has spread to three more households since they made that decision
Has already been exposed and is symptomatic, presenting publicly as unaffected
{npc} stands close to them every day. They've said nothing
The quarantine order they're enforcing doesn't apply to shipments from a specific merchant they have a financial relationship with
That merchant's last shipment arrived four days ago
Has been selling access to unquarantined routes for cash. The price goes up as the desperation increases
Three of the people who paid are now symptomatic. They know where they got through
Falsified the initial case count to prevent panic, and now the actual count is far higher than the official record
{faction} is about to do their own independent count as part of a resource audit
Is hoarding medicinal {commodity} that should have been distributed, rationing it for their own use and close associates
The official stores are now visibly insufficient. Someone will investigate where the gap is
Has already committed to supporting a specific claimant in private, while publicly presenting as neutral
They made the same commitment to the other claimant last week
Knows the deceased's actual wishes regarding succession. They were told privately and have chosen not to share them
The wishes favour neither of the current claimants. Sharing them would destabilise everything and serve justice simultaneously
Has a document that would legally resolve the succession, in a direction that would require them to give up their current position
They've been sitting on it for three weeks. The longer they wait, the harder the explanation
Was promised a specific appointment by one claimant in exchange for a public endorsement they have not yet delivered
The claimant is now asking why the endorsement hasn't come. The answer is that the other claimant offered more
Has been quietly removing records from the archive that would complicate the succession in ways they prefer not to see complicated
{npc} manages the archive and has noticed the gaps. They've raised it with {faction}
The attacks are not random. They sent a patrol into that territory three weeks ago and provoked something. No one came back. They filed a false report
The survivors' families believe their people died in an accident. They've been asking questions
Has been negotiating with the creature threat on their own authority, and the terms they've offered include access rights the settlement doesn't know they gave
{npc} intercepted one communication. They don't fully understand what they read
The {commodity} operation they authorised six months ago disturbed a nesting site. The attacks started three weeks later
The connection is in the geographic data. Someone with the right maps will make it
Has been selling information about patrol schedules to an outside party who claims to be a monster hunter, and may not be
The last three ambushes hit patrols on days that weren't in the standard rotation
Their private property (inherited land beyond the last fields) is part of the territory being contested. They've been subtly steering the hunting parties away from it
Two defenders died in an area they should have been sent to protect
Has been quietly forwarding a share of the taxes they collect to the insurgency (as insurance, not conviction)
If the authority survives, this is treason. If the insurgency wins, it is not enough. They bet on neither side and owe both
Wrote the anonymous manifesto that gave the insurgency its language, and has since publicly condemned it more than once
{npc} recognised the phrasing. They have said nothing, but they read the condemnation with a strange expression
Is the insurgency's contact inside the council, and has been feeding it exactly the information that keeps the fighting away from their own district
Three other districts have suffered. Theirs has not. Someone is beginning to notice the pattern
Ordered a crackdown that killed people who had nothing to do with the insurgency, then falsified the reports to record them as insurgents
The families know their dead were innocent. One of them has kept everything
Has already negotiated their own safe passage with the insurgency's leadership in exchange for opening a gate on a night yet to be named
The night is close. {faction} still believes this person is loyal
Knows the insurgency is being funded from outside the settlement, by a party the authority itself has been quietly dealing with
Exposing the funding exposes the deal. They have been sitting on both halves for months
Has been moving insurgent fighters and sealed messages through the underways (the dug tunnels beneath the settlement), one cellar-mouth at a time
The warren has no map, but {npc} has walked it. If the authority ever forces one, this person's own route becomes the confession
Has been selling residency papers and gate-passes to newcomers who cannot legally settle, at a price that rises with their desperation
The register is falsified in a pattern anyone auditing arrivals would find. An audit has been requested
Diverted the relief meant for the newcomer camp into a private arrangement, and the shortfall is being blamed on the newcomers themselves
People in the camp are dying of the shortfall. The blame is holding, for now
Is themselves a newcomer, arrived a decade ago under a false history that the current upheaval is threatening to expose
The people they would rule against for lying are lying no more than they once did
Has been quietly buying up the houses the newcomers need, through a third party, and letting them at a price that rises with every arrival
The tenants have begun comparing what they pay. The third party's name will not survive the first honest question
Knows the migration was triggered by something upstream (a failed harvest, a war, a purge) that {faction} helped cause and has been concealing
The newcomers carry the proof in their own stories, if anyone here thinks to listen
Signed the order closing the settlement to further arrivals, then made a paid exception for one group now already settled inside
{npc} was turned away the same week. They saw the paid group admitted. They have not forgotten a face
Has been under-declaring the settlement's stores to the requisition officers and selling the concealed {commodity} to both armies
The next requisition will physically count what the ledgers claim. The ledgers are wrong by a wagon-train
Falsified the conscription rolls to keep their own household's men home, filling the quota with the names of the poor and the friendless
Several of those men are dead. Their families were told it was an honour
Took a private share of the war contracts that made the settlement rich, routed through a merchant house that does not exist on paper
The house's accounts exist somewhere. A rival contractor has been looking for exactly this
Knows the war is going worse than the settlement has been told, and has been quietly moving their family and their wealth ahead of the news
{npc} helped load the last cart. They asked no questions then. They are asking them now
Authorised the seizure of a rival's property as a 'war measure', on evidence they invented
The rival's heir survived the war the seizure was meant to fund, and has come home with the original documents
Has been feeding the enemy's quartermasters the same false supply figures they feed their own, playing both requisitions for the skim
When the war ends, both sides will reconcile their books. The discrepancy points one direction
Converted publicly to the ascendant faith while still practising the old one in private, and has been informing on other secret adherents to prove their sincerity
The people they named trusted them. Some are already ruined. One has not yet been named
Holds the deeds and endowments of the old religious institution, which they were meant to transfer, and has been quietly keeping them in the confusion
Both faiths claim the properties. Only this person knows the documents never actually moved
Engineered the 'miracle' that tipped the settlement toward the new faith, and knows exactly how it was done
The apparatus still exists, hidden. Anyone who found it would unmake the conversion and every career built on it
Was a senior figure in the old faith and surrendered its secrets (its finances, its sanctuary lists, its private sins) to the new one to secure a place
The sanctuary lists named people now being hunted. {npc} was on a list this person handed over
Has been forging records to erase the old faith's marriages, oaths, and legitimacies, retroactively unmaking inheritances and alliances
One of the unmade legitimacies belongs to a family with the means to check the originals
Knows the conversion was arranged for reasons that had nothing to do with faith (a debt, a marriage, a foreign hand) and holds the correspondence that proves it
{faction} would pay to bury it. The other faith would pay more to reveal it
Has been in secret contact with the revolt's leadership, brokering terms the governing power has refused to authorise
If the negotiation is discovered they hang as a traitor; if it fails the settlement burns. They have told no one
Owned a share of the slave market and has been destroying the records of exactly whom they owned before those records can be turned against them
{npc} kept a copy. They have not yet decided what to do with it
Freed and armed a group of the enslaved themselves, quietly, before the revolt began, for reasons they have not disclosed and cannot now defend
Those they armed are among the revolt's leaders. If it is known who gave them steel, the answer implicates this person entirely
Knows the revolt began because of a specific atrocity the authorities ordered and then denied
The order exists in writing. This person filed it. They have been trying to make it disappear for six days
Has already arranged to flee with their wealth the moment the revolt breaks through, abandoning the defence they are publicly organising
Those holding out are doing so partly on faith in this person's leadership. That faith is misplaced
Is protecting one specific enslaved person for private reasons, at the cost of intelligence that would help contain the revolt
The person they are protecting is close to the revolt's leadership. The connection would ruin them if it were traced
Has been running the enslaved out through the underways for weeks before the revolt broke, using smugglers' tunnels no census ever recorded
Those they moved are now among the revolt's fighters, and the tunnel-keepers know exactly who paid for the passage
